analysis_md:
解答 $L:\begin{cases}x=a\cos^3t\\y=a\sin^3t\end{cases}$，且 $\sqrt{x_t'^2+y_t'^2}=3a\sin t\cos t$，

$$
M=\int_L\rho(x,y)ds=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}(a\cos^3t+a^2\sin^3t\cos^3t+a\sin^3t)\sqrt{x_t'^2+y_t'^2}\,dt
$$

$$
=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}(a\cos^3t+a^2\sin^3t\cos^3t+a\sin^3t)\cdot3a\sin t\cos tdt
$$

$$
=3a^2\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sin t\cos^4tdt+3a^3\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sin^4t\cos^4tdt+3a^2\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sin^4t\cos tdt
$$

$$
=\frac{6a^2}{5}+3a^3\left[\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}(\sin^4t-2\sin^6t+\sin^8t)dt\right]
$$

$$
=\frac{6}{5}a^2+\frac{9\pi}{256}a^3.
$$
